notes: Maps changed paths to the narrowest truthful proof-lane set. Consumed by tools/proof_lane_select.mjs.

Tier semantics: 'frozen' areas are trusted between full sweeps and excluded from sprint-mode defaults; tier NEVER exempts an area from diff-triggered selection — touching a frozen area (directly, via crate closure, or via also_triggers) re-arms its lanes for that run.

Re-declare tiers at sprint boundaries: the current frontier's areas are 'active', completed-and-untouched surfaces are 'frozen'. Frozen areas must cite registry capabilities that are all status=complete (validated by test:proof-lane-contract).
Path matching: entries ending in '/' or '.' are prefixes; anything else is an exact file match. Longest match wins.

A canonical crate area uses 'crate' to own its reverse Cargo closure. A specialized build-input area may instead use 'closure_crate' to participate in that closure without competing for canonical crate ownership.
also_triggers encodes cross-boundary blast radius the crate DAG cannot see (e.g. strict-wire change 32e8623b broke ~10 proof tools and frontend transport).

Generated-artifact lanes declare source input and checked-in output path patterns plus a canonical write_command. Either side directly arms the freshness lane, independent of area boundaries; every concrete output has one lane owner.
Manifest lanes are executable leaves. Human aggregate npm aliases stay outside this table; selected leaves are deduplicated by canonical execution key.

Every cargo test leaf declares assertion_targets and selects only those library, binary, or integration-test targets. The proof contract rejects missing targets and targets whose source contains no test declaration; rustdoc remains compilation coverage owned by workspace Clippy because the workspace doctest inventory is empty.

Every leaf declares exact execution metadata. Cargo target access, browsers, frontend worktrees, container engines, network access, Postgres administration, disposable databases, and artifact directories are scheduled as independent resources.
Push mode is the touched closure plus a measured bounded sentinel set. Sprint mode adds every active-tier area; full mode selects every declared lane.

Full execution is content-addressed: a lane owned exclusively by frozen areas may reuse an immutable passing result whose key still matches canonical crate proof-graph sources or specialized explicit sources, owned fixtures, migrations, dependency locks, toolchain, exact execution graph, and proof-runner implementation. --mode full --force executes every lane.

Proof-cache maintenance receipts are audited on every push. Recovery from an interrupted or failed application always creates a new current-state plan and immutable linkage; attempted plans are never replayed.
